title: Marines & Sailors Dig Trenches to Fight Drone Threats
text:
SKRUNDA, Latvia, 2025-06-18 21:42:00
defensive Trenches in Focus U.S. Marines and Latvian Army troops are collaborating on exercises to fortify against potential drone threats.
U.S. Marines and Latvian troops trained together in Latvia. They built trenches and fortifications to counter drone threats. The training was part of the larger Baltic Operations exercise. In Latvia, U.S. Marines and Latvian Army troops recently teamed up to construct trenches and fortifications, preparing for drone warfare. This hands-on training is crucial for adapting to modern combat scenarios and enhancing force protection.
U.S. Navy Seabees assigned to naval Construction Battalion 14 showcase a trench reinforcement project to senior enlisted leaders.(Chief Petty Officer Justin Stumberg/navy) Building resilience in the Field The training,which took place in skrunda,Latvia,involved Marines from the 8th Engineer Support Battalion and Seabees with Naval Construction Battalion 14. They worked alongside Latvian Army troops to construct trenches and fortifications. The goal was to prepare for potential drone threats and test new battlefield tactics.
“These field fortifications are built to reduce detection, limit exposure to unmanned systems, and enhance force protection across the battlespace,” said Lt. j.g. Wiatt Lewis of Naval Construction battalion 14.
The service members used lumber from the Latvian Army’s field-deployable sawmill to reinforce trench walls and build overhead cover and concealment.
did you know? -Field-deployable sawmills allow troops to rapidly convert local timber into construction materials, reducing reliance on external supply chains and accelerating fortification efforts.
Part of a Bigger Picture the exercise was part of the Baltic Operations exercise, or BALTOPS, an annual event in the Baltic region. It is indeed focused on maritime and air scenarios.
Reader question: -How might advancements in drone technology further influence the design and construction of defensive fortifications in the future?
The war in Ukraine has underscored the importance of such preparations. Trenches and field fortifications are crucial for protection against drones. They’ve become a regular part of combat, even in major attacks.
Small ground units must contend with drone threats, too.These devices can spot troops for strikes and carry munitions.
“We are always thinking about our visibility from above, the effects of thermal detection, and how to keep the position secure from multiple angles,” said staff Sgt. Austin Leigh, a combat engineer with the 8th Engineer Support Battalion.
The role of Drones in Modern Warfare: A Deep Dive The training exercises in Latvia, as highlighted in the previous sections, focused on preparing for modern warfare, specifically against the threat of drones. Beyond building trenches, the increasing prevalence of unmanned aerial systems (UAS) necessitates a deeper understanding of their capabilities and corresponding defensive strategies.
drones, or unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs), now perform a multitude of roles in combat, transitioning from simple reconnaissance platforms to instruments of offensive action. These roles demand constant adaptation,as the technology rapidly evolves. This adaptability is critical for military forces preparing for potential conflicts.
The Multifaceted Threat Landscape Drones present a complex challenge because of their diverse capabilities. They can be used for:
Reconnaissance and Surveillance: Drones offer real-time intelligence on enemy positions and movements. target Acquisition: They can identify and pinpoint targets for artillery strikes and other weapons systems. Direct Attack: Some drones are armed with missiles, bombs, or other payloads for offensive operations. Electronic Warfare: Certain UAS can be used to jam communications or disrupt enemy radar systems. Logistics and Resupply: Drones can be used to deliver supplies and equipment to troops in the field. This versatility is why the U.S. Marines and Latvian Army are emphasizing drone defense. Effective defensive strategies must therefore address a range of threats.
How can defensive fortifications counter drone threats? Defensive fortifications need to incorporate strategies for camouflage, electronic countermeasures, and physical protection. Furthermore, incorporating these features requires a cohesive defensive strategy encompassing awareness, detection, and response capabilities.
The role of anti-drone technology is increasing. Active systems like radar and electronic jammers can identify and neutralize incoming drones. Passive defenses, like camouflage and physical barriers, are also essential.
Beyond Trenches: Innovative Approaches While trenches remain essential, the landscape of drone warfare demands innovative solutions. Military engineers are exploring several areas:
Enhanced Camouflage: Employing materials and techniques that reduce thermal and visual signatures. Drone Detection Systems: Integrating radar, acoustic sensors, and visual recognition software. Directed Energy Weapons: Utilizing lasers or high-powered microwaves to disable or destroy drones. Cyber Warfare: Hacking and disrupting drone control systems. The U.S. military and its allies are actively researching and deploying these technologies to maintain a strategic advantage. Field exercises like those in Latvia are critical for testing and integrating these advancements. The goal is not merely to survive drone attacks but to minimize their impact on operations, protecting our troops and ensuring mission success.
Practical Tips for Enhanced Force protection: Smaller, adaptable steps can improve force protection. Here are some steps that can be taken to reduce detection and exposure to drone threats:
Master Camouflage Techniques: Utilize camouflage nets, natural concealment, and deceptive decoys. Maintain Radio Silence: Limit radio transmissions to avoid detection by drone-based signal intelligence. Use Electronic countermeasures: Consider deploying devices to jam drone control signals. Establish Drone Watch: Designate personnel to scan the skies for approaching drones and trigger warnings. Practice Dispersion: Avoid clustering personnel and equipment to minimize exposure to attacks. Train Regularly: conduct frequent drills to familiarize troops with drone threats and response procedures. Myth vs. Fact: Drones and defensive Fortifications Myth Fact Drones are only a threat to large units. Small ground units are also vulnerable, needing to defend against surveillance and small-scale attacks. Camouflage is no longer effective against modern drones. Effective camouflage, using thermal and visual countermeasures, remains a crucial element of drone defense. Anti-drone technology is a perfect solution. anti-drone systems can be spoofed; a multi-layered approach including physical defenses is essential. Frequently Asked Questions Q: What types of drones are most risky in modern conflict?
A: Small, commercially available drones, easy to operate and challenging to detect, pose a meaningful threat due to their accessibility and the range of payloads they may carry.
Q: How can troops mitigate the threat posed by enemy drones in combat zones?
A: Troops can mitigate the threat by practicing strict camouflage, using electronic warfare countermeasures, setting up drone-watch patrols, and practicing dispersion.
